tweet.text:
A 35B language model. Running on an iPhone. Peak memory: 1–2.5 GB.

No cloud. No remote server. No desktop GPU.

someone open-sourced Edge0, a framework for running large AI models fully on-device.

This is not a demo of a heavily cut-down model. It is a way to keep a large model intact while shrinking the working set that actually lives in memory. The full weights can stay on storage. Only the parameters needed for the current step enter RAM.

1. First release includes:
- Runtime and inference code: https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0/
- 8B model: https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Edge0-8B-A1B-preview
- 35B model: https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0/

Built for phones, laptops, PCs, and robots. Fast. Private. Fully local.

2. Why this matters

For years, a 35B-class model almost always meant the cloud—or a machine with a large GPU. On-device AI was reserved for much smaller models.
Edge0 attacks a different problem: not “how do we make the model smaller,” but “how do we keep the active memory small.”
The result is a large model with a small working set.

3. How a 35B model fits in 1–2.5 GB

In simple terms:
The full model stays in storage.
Only the parameters needed for the current step are loaded into memory.
The next parameters are prepared while the current step is running.
Memory is reused instead of loading the entire model at once.
Under the hood, Edge0 is an open-source streaming MoE inference framework for devices with tight memory budgets.

- SSD expert offload
MoE expert weights are memory-mapped on SSD and streamed on demand. Hot experts stay cached in memory. Long-tail experts are prefetched layer by layer.
- Prerouter routing prediction
Edge0 predicts the next token’s expert routes one step ahead, overlapping SSD reads with the current forward pass.
- Parallel LoRA
LoRA adapters are applied at runtime rather than merged. One read-only base model can serve multiple adapter sets.

Put simply: the full model lives on storage; only the weights needed for each step are in active memory.

4. Who it’s for
Private assistants. Offline agents. On-device robotics. Any product that cannot send user data to the cloud.
